mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 8.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a weak labor market that may prompt central bank intervention, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate policy support.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 8.0% for two consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales growth indicate a weakening consumer demand cycle, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production, the S&P 500 tends to underperform as manufacturing slowdowns signal weakening economic activity and lower corporate profits, leading to negative returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as bond yields rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% YoY, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising quarterly GDP growth rate indicates expanding economic activity that supports corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the equity market prices in stronger economic fundamentals.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth is positive, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly job gains exceed 100,000, it signals a strengthening labor market that may lead to higher wage growth and inflation, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate monetary tightening.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 100,000, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In the context of a housing market recovery, rising housing starts signal increased consumer confidence and economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the equity market anticipates stronger consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is rising, or Rank IC for HOUST rise < 0.03 over 3-year window.
